title: LTR divergence, body size and reproductive strategy
datasets: Frozen Figure 2 profile exports; Figure 12 scores, predictions, contrasts and omnibus tests
legend: Within-LTR low-divergence representation differs among reproductive groups in an exploratory phylogenetic comparison. (a) All 34 species are shown as gray divergence profiles; colored curves are equal-weight reproductive-group means. Each 1-percentage-point bin contains its percentage of all RepeatMasker-aligned hit bp; bins 0–49 are displayed with missing order/bin combinations zero-filled. (b) All 34 named species retain the shared phylogenetic order. The within-LTR fraction is LTR hit bp in bins 0–4 divided by all LTR hit bp across all divergence bins. It separates relative profile shape from total LTR representation; it is not genome occupancy, insertion age, or transposition rate. (c) Stored Pagel-lambda PGLS predictions from logit(within-LTR fraction) ~ strategy + log10(maximum SVL), restricted to each group's observed SVL range; bands are conditional 95% intervals. (d) Stored raw-logit contrasts and 95% t intervals compare each group with aquatic eggs, before and after SVL adjustment. The adjusted omnibus likelihood-ratio P is 0.000568 (2 df). The adjusted terrestrial-versus-aquatic contrast is 0.439 (95% CI 0.061–0.818); the direct-development contrast is −0.448 (−1.037–0.142). Strategies were expert-coded after PCA inspection; group sizes are not counts of independent evolutionary transitions. Contrasts remain exploratory and conditional on the source tree and fitted lambda. The within-LTR fraction covaries with dnaPipeTE unresolved fraction (unadjusted Spearman rho = −0.452, P = 0.0072), but not clearly with aligned sample fraction (rho = −0.161, P = 0.362). These cross-pipeline quality associations do not establish the origin of the group pattern. Abbreviations: LTR, long terminal repeat; SVL, snout–vent length; PGLS, phylogenetic generalized least squares; CI, confidence interval.
alt_text: All-species repeat profiles and named within-LTR fractions accompany body-size predictions and phylogenetic strategy contrasts.
